note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Embedding-level mixing as a controlled probe of language-mixed queries, and what it reveals

nodes.name: Mixed queries untested
nodes.description: Multilingual retrievers are typically developed and evaluated with monolingual or cross-lingual queries, so mixed-language query behavior is largely untested in standard benchmarks.

nodes.name: LLM word-level mixing is costly
nodes.description: LLM-generated word-level code-switching does not guarantee successful generation and requires a separate generation for each mixing ratio, making ratio-controlled study resource-intensive.

nodes.name: Embedding-level mixing proposed
nodes.description: Language-mixed queries are represented as a convex combination (ratio lambda, then L2-normalized) of the two monolingual query-translation embeddings, giving precise ratio control without repeated LLM generation.

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.description: Experiments use BGE-M3 on mMARCO with 35 language pairs from 13 languages, a filtered set of 1,484 long queries, and three document settings (L1-only, L2-only, L1+L2), giving 105 groups scored by nDCG@10.

nodes.name: Embed-mix tracks word-mix trends
nodes.description: On EN-ZH, embedding mixing matches word-level mixing trends in all three document settings (no new interior peak on EN+ZH) and attains higher nDCG, since it avoids word-mixing noise from generation variability and tokenization/LID errors.

nodes.name: Mixing often helps
nodes.description: Optimal embedding-level mixing ratios beat the best monolingual endpoint in 88/105 groups (83.8%), with mean gain +0.70, range -0.34 to +2.92, and 66/105 reliably positive.

nodes.name: Largest and worst cases
nodes.description: The largest gain is EN-AR on AR documents (+2.9203 at lambda*=50) and the most negative is EN-ZH on EN+ZH documents (-0.3359 at lambda*=10).

nodes.name: Mixing helps only without English documents
nodes.description: When English is absent from the index all groups have positive gain (average +0.95), whereas with English documents gains cluster near zero (mean -0.04) so pure English queries are best.

nodes.name: English effect is asymmetric
nodes.description: Adding English to ZH queries improves ZH-document retrieval (+1.72 at lambda*=50), but adding ZH to EN queries consistently worsens English-document retrieval, so English overrides document-query similarity.

nodes.name: English is strongest partner
nodes.description: For every one of the 13 non-English document languages, English yields the largest mixing gain among tested partner languages, by a large margin.

nodes.name: English pretraining dominance hypothesis
nodes.description: The authors hypothesize English acts as a universal anchor because web-corpus imbalance gives the English subspace the most robust representations.

nodes.name: Typology correlates weakly
nodes.description: Without English-in-documents effects (44 non-English settings), typological distance has a moderate negative correlation with gains (Spearman rho=-0.405); script, family and resource effects are weak.

nodes.name: Headroom effect
nodes.description: Gain is negatively correlated with the better endpoint's score (rho=-0.607), driven by English-document settings (rho=-0.684), weak when English is excluded (rho=-0.117).

nodes.name: Findings robust across models
nodes.description: Patterns hold across model families and Qwen3 scales; scaling raises monolingual scores and shrinks gains but English remains the strongest partner and mixing does not help English retrieval.

nodes.name: Deployment guidance
nodes.description: For English-inclusive indices systems should default to pure English queries, while for non-English indices embedding mixing is an effective test-time augmentation to improve recall.

isolated_nodes.name: Mixing preserves entities but is not lexical
isolated_nodes.description: Interpolation with English helps even for strictly monolingual queries without English loanwords, so the advantage is not just surface-level lexical matching (Appx C.3).

isolated_nodes.name: Low-resource generalization
isolated_nodes.description: The conclusions generalize to extremely low-resource languages in resource bands 0-2 (Appx C.2).

isolated_nodes.name: Future directions
isolated_nodes.description: Future work should study naturally mixed queries and interpolation of multiple languages simultaneously.

structural_reasoning: Method motivation (costly word-level mixing) leads to the embedding-mix probe, validated against word mixing, whose global result is then decomposed by English dominance, partner language, metadata and robustness, ending in deployment guidance.
